Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating Liam, a 7-month-old male who has been under my care since concerns first arose during a routine check at two months of age. 

Liam is currently interactive and meeting gross motor milestones. Physical examination today is reassuring: he is afebrile with normal vital signs, clear lung fields, and normal cardiac auscultation without murmurs. His abdomen is soft without masses or organomegaly, and he displays no dysmorphic traits. Family history is negative for early renal disease, and he is up to date on all infant immunizations. 

Our recent investigations revealed compromised baseline renal function, evidenced by an elevated serum creatinine of 0.74 mg/dL. His blood intact PTH is substantially increased, and his circulating magnesium concentration remains depressed at 1.1 mg/dL. Urinalysis demonstrates significant spilled protein, with a spot protein-to-creatinine ratio of 1.6 mg/mg. Subsequent urine chemistries also highlighted a marked overexcretion of uric acid. In addition, an ultrasound of the kidneys demonstrated extensive medullary calcium deposits bilaterally.

Given this constellation of abnormalities, I would greatly appreciate your assessment and guidance regarding ongoing clinical management.

Sincerely,
Dr. Evelyn Carter
General Pediatrics
